customize.desc: One of the many bards of Mondstadt, who freely wanders the city's streets and alleys.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>Character Story 5</color>
The Anemo Archon cannot take credit for everything in Mondstadt.
Credit should be given where credit is due, I shall sing now the praises of things beauteous and true:
We thank the West Wind, whose enduring caress
Brings the blossoms of Spring, by whose scent we are blessed.
Finches, ducks, rabbits and boars,
Mondstadt's revival bid them thrive evermore.
In summer the lion walks the plains,
No words one finds to praise it but these:
Do you sweat out your water to make way for wine?
Comes the heat of the summer from your mane of sunshine?
The mountain mouths and gorges low like drunkards wayward lie...
But the East Wind cares not, for it doesn't walk — it flies!
Over the fruit trees it brushes low,
And its wings bring the harvest of things that grow.
The North Wind in the silent forest slumbers,
And around it pace the wolves in their numbers.
Though most have never a glimpse of them seen, for the Wind knows that none is of winter too keen,
Yet the Anemo Archon glimpses and sees, that it dreams each night of warm reverie.
—As the four seasons in turn shall say their piece, so the four winds too shall never cease.
Of course, to look at it differently, I am the one who should be credited here, and not they.
Credits should be given where credits belong — if not for the bard who pens the song, then who shall ensure that these tales are passed on?

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>Character Story 1</color>
Razor lives among the wolves night and day.
All of them are as close with Razor as they could possibly be. Which wolf has the loudest howl, which wolf runs the fastest, which wolf is the best at ambushing — there isn't a wolf Razor doesn't know.
He can sense the mood of the wind, smell a scent from miles away, and knows many practical applications for plants of all kinds. The one thing he can't bring to mind is the faces of his parents.
What kind of people were they? No matter how hard he tries, he cannot remember.
His memory starts after his life with the wolves had already begun. The wolves took him in as part of their "Lupical" — a word he was taught by someone else, which means family.

customize.text: Lupus Boreas

More than three thousand years ago, far away in the wild wastelands later called Nod-Krai, a lone wolf wandered. He was once a wolf king, leading his pack on the hunt, in battle, and in the search for a home. He had led the way as they ran across open plains, navigated through abandoned ruins, and passed through the domains of monsters and the Seelie. The wolf-king grew older with each passing day, and the other wolves gradually dispersed. As time went by, the wolf pack's history faded into distant memory until finally only the aged wolf-king remained, the sole survivor of its pack. As he walked from the north and passed the palace of long-gone angels, the sounds of music caught his attention. The world had never heard such a pleasant song from birds or insects, and the wolf decided to enter the castle. Inside, he saw a fair maiden strumming at her instrument. Her skin was ashen white, and her head was bowed down, her slender fingers gently stroking the fragile strings of the lute as she played a long-forgotten and mournful melody. The maiden was the first angel, the first daughter of the Heavenly Principles and the Goddess of the Dawnstar. Six thousand years ago, she, together with a voyager from distant worlds, decided to go against the laws of the Heavenly Principles, for which she was deprived of her name and separated from the voyager, and the angels were cursed.

<color=#ffffffd9>"The chirping of insects on a long-gone autumn night is the chorus of exiles, singing mankind's most ancient song as they live out their plight..."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Stripped of all that the body once held close and the soul once held dear, songs and memories are all that now remain of yesteryear."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"The last singers, the first Seelie, they played their final tune in the hall of angels."</color>

The wolf, enchanted by the angel's song, immediately forgot his hunger, thirst, and loneliness. He understood every word, every letter, and every note, but the maiden's language was unfamiliar to him. She explained that in the distant past, it had been a song created by angels for humans, but now they sang it to mourn over their fate. After this, the wolf began to clumsily sing along, his voice filled with sorrow. And although the angel considered the song ugly, she allowed the wolf to sing along with her. The song of the wolf and the angel echoed through the halls of the old palace. It is said that to this day, adventurers who pass by this place still hear a strange yet harmonious melody sounding from within.
For a while, the wolf remained with the angel. Although he could not speak, he gazed at her as if she were a heavenly light, yearning for her song like a parched servant longs for the refreshing rain of spring. The angel was grateful that the wolf had brightened her loneliness and named him Boreas, "North Wind." After many days, the wolf gained wisdom, intelligence, and knowledge and began to treat others with kindness and sincerity. Even human words would come from its mouth. One day, Boreas turned to the angel, calling her Mother, and said, <color=#ffffffd9>"I will go to the South, where the people are poor and lowly, yet the cities are large and fortified. I will make them prosperous."</color> The angel gave him her blessing, and he, receiving this power, and his kin left the temple. Traveling south, he reached Mondstadt, where he became the King of the North Wind, Andrius.

customize.text: Great Wolf King of the North

Nearly three thousand years ago, the Great Wolf King of the North waged war against the ruler of Old Mondstadt, the God of Storm, Decarabian. He froze the land and forced Decarabian to create storm walls around Old Mondstadt (now Stormterror's Lair). The King of the North Wind could not penetrate these walls, and Decarabian looked down from the top of his tower upon his subjects, whose backs were stiffened by the wind. 2,600 years ago, the Mondstadters, along with Decarabian's slave, a nameless bard, a wind spirit, and the Storm God's former warrior, rose up in rebellion and overthrew the tyrant. When the Storm God was defeated, Boreas realized that the freezing northern winds could only extinguish life, not ignite it, so he withdrew his forces to protect this land and its people. He didn't want his refuge to be like Decarabian's.

After entrusting the people of Mondstadt to the new god, Barbatos, who had received the divine power after the tyrant's death, the King of the North Wind returned north to Nod-Krai. There, in the empty palace of the first angel, the great wolf closed his eyes and fell into slumber. Five hundred winters gave way to five hundred springs until a knight from the cold lands disturbed his peace. The nameless knight asked Boreas to accompany him on a journey south to see more of the land that had almost vanished from his memory. The King of the North Wind couldn't deny the man's sincere request, so he split his soul into two parts and once again left his home. One half remained to sleep near Lake Amsvartnir, while the other set out for Mondstadt under the name Boreas. Since Boreas' form was unstable at the beginning of his journey, he left behind many Wolf Spirit fragments along the way with the knight.
When the knight who became known as the Wolf Knight and Andrius returned to Mondstadt nearly a thousand years ago, the people had only recently regained their freedom from the tyranny of the aristocracy and were under the rule of a young order, the Knights of Favonius. The free wolf hated the city walls and the smell of fire, so he raced through forests and fields, following the knight. Andrius and the knight slew evil creatures that plagued the surrounding villages. One day, a snake demon arrived on Mondstadt's shores from the sea beyond the horizon, following the current of warmth and peace. In the early days of the Knights of Favonius, when they were still weak, the nameless knight left the city to hunt demons for the price of a single silver coin. The scent of blood and carrion rotting on the beach attracted thousands of falcons, who circled for days. This is how Falcon Coast got its name. When people begged the knight for help, they asked about the payment, and he merely requested a toast. But when people asked his name, he paused and replied, <color=#ffffffd9>"Then thou should toast my companion instead. 'Boreas' is his name."</color> Thus, the knight became known as Knight Boreas.

Boreas, seeing the ice and snow give way to green plains and hearing laughter and song in the once-dark city, addressed the Anemo Archon: <color=#ffffffd9>"So, this is the world the humans dreamed of."</color> And though the knight's journey was not yet over, Boreas chose to bid it farewell here. He cast off his physical form, taking the form of a spirit wolf. His wisdom flowed into the earth, offering his entire being to the world, becoming the protector of Mondstadt. Laying down his sword as a gravestone, the Knight of Boreas buried the Wolf in the remote countryside. The Knight of Boreas then left the city behind, living the wandering life of a lone wolf. When Vennessa summoned the Four Winds, Andrius became the Wolf of the North and the guardian of Wolfendom. Since then, the Wolf of the North has been the name of both Lupus Boreas himself and the Knights of Boreas, chosen warriors recognized by the King of the North Winds. Each served as a link between Mondstadt and Boreas and received a portion of the wolf's power in their weapons. The soul of a wolf is as unyielding as ice, and his people once drew great strength and wisdom from the Wolf Spirit. But human hearts and flesh cannot contain the soul of a god, and attempting to place the Wolf Spirit in a human vessel would slowly devour their sense of self, even if Lupus Boreas did not intend for that to happen. That's why Lupus Boreas developed the technique of imbuing weapons with his soul. It is his way of blessing his human lupical with the Wolf Spirit's protection.
<color=#ffffffd9>"A weapon once of common iron, now through friendship turned divine, twixt man and wolf a bond was made, a power born within the blade..."</color>

More than five hundred years ago, a mechanism called the "Field Tiller" accidentally ended up in Andrius's arena, and he mistook the mechanism for a brave man who challenged him. The machine could not think, but every part of it was designed for killing and fighting. It could spin, fly high into the air, and shoot fireballs. In the end, Andrius was able to defeat the machine, but it managed to leave the arena before falling. For the people of ancient Mondstadt, the "Field Tiller" became the "Tyrant's Final Fury," as they could not understand the true nature of the mechanism. This machine was the prototype for all the Ruin Guards made in Khaenri'ah and possessed the Eye of the first Field Tiller, with the help of which the Abyss Order, opposed to the Seven Kingdoms, tried to create a mechanical deity to overthrow the gods of Celestia from their thrones.

Nowadays, the wolves of Wolvendom have almost no contact with people, but one day they accepted a child into their pack, later named Razor, whom they consider their "Lupical," that is, family. One day, the Abyss Order wanted Andrius to serve them, and in return, they promised the spirit to return his divine powers. The Abyss Herald attempted to perform a ritual to possess the mind of the King of the North, just as the Abyss mage once poisoned the mind of the Dragon of the East, Dvalin. The Herald lured Andrius under the pretense of challenging him to battle but was stopped by Razor and the Traveler. Although Andrius doesn't usually want Razor to interfere with the pack's problems, when Wolvendom was attacked by the Rift Hounds, he allowed him to hunt them. The wolf pack, eager to protect the young man, went with him, and together they managed to drive the hounds away, albeit briefly.

customize.text: Knights of Boreas

When the Wolf Knight first arrived in Mondstadt, he commissioned a blacksmith to forge a new sword and paid him with a handful of coins marked with a seal he could never recognize. The blacksmith, who had previously forged swords exclusively for the nobility, chose to gift the knight a sword, believing that everyone in Mondstadt should defend their freedom. From then on, the blacksmith's son, Ravenwood, followed the nameless knight like a shadow. Most often, he watched him practice with his sword or listened to stories of a place where flowers never withered, where rivers ran with mead, and along their banks once stood a warrior kingdom that had since vanished from the world. There, warriors who often sang of devotion and honor bowed before power and gold, willingly offering their blades to a greedy tyrant.
When the nameless knight left Mondstadt, Ravenwood decided to continue his work. It is said that freedom is born of great sacrifice, yet the comfort that follows often leads back to servitude. At that time, the order's commandments were still remembered, but former comrades had already broken their oaths, seeking refuge once again in the embrace of the old aristocracy. In those uncertain times, a blacksmith's son took up his sword and set out into the wasteland. <color=#ffffffd9>"Once lost, neither freedom nor the courage to die for it can be reclaimed. Cherish your virtue while it still endures."</color> A few days later, a knight in a tattered cloak appeared at the fortress gates. He wielded his heavy, fearsome sword at his opponent, and it seemed as if the gods themselves were helping him. One of the elders recognized his style, the same one once used by a knight calling himself "Andrius." Thus, Ravenwood became Mondstadt's new Knight of Boreas.

Another Knight of Boreas five hundred years ago was Rostam, nicknamed the "Wolf Pup." He was a peasant child who grew up with a descendant of knights, Arundolyn. When Arundolyn became the new Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, Rostam was his right-hand man. When the Cataclysm began in Teyvat and black streams of curses gushed from the ground, Rostam, Arundolyn, and Rostam's apprentice, Roland, set out to slay monsters and defend Mondstadt. Rostam, who could one day assume the position of Grand Master, fell in battle. Dying, the Wolf Pup dreamed of hearing the song of his beloved and was glad that Arundolyn and Roland were safe. The White Knight, Roland, had earned the respect of the Boreas even before he received his title. Everyone believed he would become the most powerful Knight of Boreas in history. He was truthful and principled and followed the path of justice. His armor gleamed silver, and a mirror-sheen sword hung from his hip. Whatever form injustice took, be it a man-eating beast or a distant fire, the knight raced to confront it. After so many battles, the knight no longer distinguished whether it was the enemy's blood or his own that stained his once-gleaming armor crimson. Finally, he realized that his long knightly journey through carnage had transformed him from a warrior of light on a white steed into a nightmarish, cruel monster. The White Knight became the Bloodstained Knight. Realizing there was no place for him in this world, he sought death in the very abode of monsters, the lost ancient kingdom of Khaenri'ah. In the abyss of the world, he learned of Khaenri'ah's fate through the vision of one of the Five Sinners, Vedrfolnir. Roland viewed the gods' decision as the utmost injustice, which compelled him to ally himself with the Abyss. He gave her his knowledge, his power, and everything he had.

The current and most powerful Knight of Boreas is the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius, Varka. He possesses such power that he could master the two-handed claymore and longsword technique created by the Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius 500 years ago. Because almost no one could master this technique, no records of it remained, and in all of Mondstadt, only Lupus Boreas could have seen it in action. As a young knight, Varka set out to fight the King of the North. Over several days of continuous battle, the knight earned the esteem of Boreas. One day, Varka saw a fortune in a scryglass, learning of an impending black disaster in Nod-Krai. Since Andrius's soul was also in Nod-Krai, Varka organized an expedition to learn more about the potential threat and its connection to Lupus Boreas and to protect Mondstadt.

When the Abyssal manifestation in Nod-Krai, called the Wild Hunt, lost its leader, Sinner Rerir, the Abyss created a copy of the Bloodstained Knight from his memories. As Roland was a mere mortal, lacking even a fraction of the Sinner's power, the Abyss merged with the soul of Andrius, who slept by Lake Amsvartnir, imbuing "Roland" with divine power. To stop the Wild Hunt, the current Knight of Boreas, Varka, devised a plan to free Andrius's soul. The spirit of the
gave him a portion of his power and memories of merging with the Ley Lines to protect Mondstadt so that Andrius's soul would make the same decision. Furthermore, the Knight of Boreas collected Wolf Spirit fragments scattered across Nod-Krai to strengthen his resolve to merge with the Ley Lines. To deceive Roland, Varka hid the god's portion within his heart, allowing it to consume him. Thus, when the Bloodstained Knight destroyed the Knight of Boreas's sword, Varka was still able to transfer the Wolf of the North's memories to Andrius's heart. The god once again chose to merge with the Ley Lines, taking Varka and Roland with him. Thanks to letters from Varka's friends awaiting his return to Mondstadt, Knight of Boreas was able to return to reality.

value.desc:
The noblest and greatest of souls, who watches over the lupical of Wolvendom.
When the wolfpack is imperiled, it will emerge in the form of a wolf and show forth its fangs and claws.

The wolves of Wolvendom are frightening phantoms to the people of Mondstadt:
A blurred shape flashing through the forest, a chilling howl in the indeterminate distance, the creeping sense of eyes constantly nailed to their backs...
Humans rarely have the opportunity to lock their eyes with a wolf, for this is the law Lupus Boreas laid down for its race.
